subject.title: fix(sessions): persist sender metadata in user turn transcript JSONL

question: Should OpenClaw persist senderId, senderName, and senderUsername as durable __openclaw metadata for group/channel user-turn JSONL while continuing to exclude phone-number identity?
rationale: The implementation path is focused and source-supported, but persisting human participant identifiers in durable transcript state is a privacy/security-boundary choice automation should not make for maintainers.

options.title: Approve Bounded Sender Metadata
options.body: Accept senderId, senderName, and senderUsername as durable group/channel transcript metadata while keeping phone-number identity excluded.

options.title: Narrow Or Document The Boundary
options.body: Ask for a smaller field set or explicit transcript privacy documentation before changing the durable JSONL shape.

options.title: Pause Until More Live Proof
options.body: Require fresh redacted latest-head Telegram ingress proof before deciding whether this identity boundary is acceptable.

recommendation.title: Approve Bounded Sender Metadata
recommendation.body: Accept senderId, senderName, and senderUsername as durable group/channel transcript metadata while keeping phone-number identity excluded.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent branch commits on the sender metadata path, adjacent inbound-context history, and was directly pinged in the PR discussion for maintainer review.
